ops.title: evt.cmd fluent API landed WITH 7 known fail-open holes — DO NOT adopt in guards until closed
ops.body: 2026-07-19: per user directive, the evt.cmd fluent command API (cmd.py Cmd/Call/Target/Targets/Expansion + ToolRewriteEvent.cmd) is being pushed to captain-hook main and released as 11.1.0 WITH 7 adversarially-confirmed fail-open holes still open — the fix is owned by a SEPARATE agent (not this orchestrator). SAFE because evt.cmd is UNCONSUMED: no pack guard calls it yet (deletions.py still uses the old rewrite_command_occurrences visitor). The 7 holes (fail OPEN = dangerous cmd runs while API reports safe/verified/absent), full detail in note 8245d30: (1/3) tainted double-quoted shell payload not descended — bash -c "rm -rf $HOME" → calls('rm')==[]; (2) process substitution <(rm -rf /) produces no occurrence; (4) brace expansion rm {/,tmp/x} verified=True; (5) xargs stripped as transparent wrapper → zero targets vacuously verified; (6) arithmetic $((..)) dropped. HARD GATE: Phase C pack migration (deletions.py→evt.cmd, closes d026e9c) MUST NOT proceed until these are fixed and re-reviewed — adopting evt.cmd in a guard today reintroduces every bypass. Partial fix WIP preserved on branch cmd-failclosed-wip (3bb14eef). Fail-closed principle in 8245d30.
